event_name: US-Mexico border closure threat
description: President Trump threatened to close the US-Mexico border at the end of March 2019; Mexican Hass f.o.b.s rose sharply (34% on April 2, the biggest one-day jump in a decade) before he backed off the plan on April 4.

event_name: E. coli O157:H7 outbreak linked to Salinas romaine
description: CDC and FDA investigated an E. coli O157:H7 outbreak linked to romaine from the Salinas Valley, and from November 22 CDC advised consumers not to eat Salinas romaine; 167 cases in 27 states, declared over January 15, 2020.

event_name: COVID-19 restaurant closures and panic buying
description: After the March 13, 2020 national emergency declaration, restaurant closures cut foodservice demand while stockpiling lifted retail sales; IRI data showed US retail avocado dollar sales up 27% year on year in the week ending March 15.

event_name: COVID-19 restaurant closures and panic buying
description: Restaurant, school and university closures after mid-March 2020 removed foodservice demand; a Florida grower abandoned about 250 acres of cucumbers and other vegetables in early April after foodservice orders disappeared.

event_name: COVID-19 restaurant closures and panic buying
description: Foodservice lettuce sales fell almost to zero after restaurants and schools closed in mid-March 2020; a Fresno County grower plowed under more than 6 million heads of iceberg on 254 acres.

event_name: COVID-19 restaurant closures and panic buying
description: Stay-at-home orders in March-April 2020 closed restaurants and schools, which are key onion buyers, while retail demand surged; suppliers described onions as among the hottest items when COVID first hit.

event_name: Salmonella Newport outbreak linked to red onions (Thomson International)
description: FDA and CDC linked a Salmonella Newport outbreak to red onions from Thomson International, which recalled all red, yellow, white and sweet yellow onions on August 1, 2020; 1,127 cases in 48 states, declared over October 8, 2020.

event_name: INSV and soil-disease lettuce shortage in Salinas
description: Impatiens necrotic spot virus and Sclerotinia, plus August-September heat and wildfire ash, cut harvestable lettuce in the Salinas Valley in fall 2020, and Markon expected tight supplies for the rest of the Salinas season; the Grower-Shipper Association put 2020 INSV losses at about $100 million.

event_name: Pacific Northwest heat wave cuts onion crop
description: Record heat in Idaho, Oregon and Washington from late June to mid-July 2021, plus wildfire smoke, reduced yields and onion sizes in the Northwest storage crop; trade press reported tight supplies of large and red onions through the 2021-22 storage season.

event_name: Fall 2021 lettuce shortage at Salinas-Yuma transition
description: Below-average temperatures delayed the Yuma crop as late-season Salinas supply dwindled, and heavy rain in Salinas in late October and early November further cut leafy green volumes; tight supplies were expected into mid-December.

event_name: Salmonella Oranienburg outbreak linked to onions from Chihuahua (ProSource)
description: On October 20, 2021, CDC identified whole red, white and yellow onions imported from Chihuahua, Mexico and distributed by ProSource as the source of a Salmonella Oranienburg outbreak, and ProSource and Keeler Family Farms recalled them; 1,040 cases in 39 states, DC and Puerto Rico, declared over February 2, 2022. Window capped at 10 weeks.

event_name: US suspends Mexican avocado imports
description: USDA-APHIS halted inspections and all Mexican avocado imports after a threat against a US plant-safety inspector in Michoacan; imports resumed on Feb 18, 2022.

event_name: Texas enhanced border truck inspections
description: Texas Gov. Abbott ordered state troopers to inspect every commercial truck entering from Mexico from April 8, 2022, leaving at least $114 million in fresh produce stuck mainly at the Pharr-Reynosa bridge, a key avocado crossing; he effectively ended the policy on April 15 after deals with the four Mexican border states.

event_name: Wendy's romaine E. coli outbreak
description: An E. coli O157 outbreak (84 cases in MI, OH, IN, PA by late August 2022) was linked to romaine on Wendy's sandwiches; Wendy's pulled the lettuce on Aug 19, 2022; CDC declared the outbreak over on October 4, 2022.

event_name: INSV lettuce shortage in California
description: Impatiens necrotic spot virus plus hot weather cut Salinas/Central Valley lettuce yields by up to half; iceberg FOB prices peaked in October-November 2022.

event_name: Winter 2022-23 cucumber shortage
description: Fall 2022 hurricanes in Florida removed late-season cucumber volume, and cold temperatures from Christmas 2022 onward slowed Mexican and Honduran crops, leaving cucumber supplies short in January-February 2023.

event_name: Spring 2023 lettuce shortage after Salinas flooding
description: Winter 2023 storms and flooding delayed Salinas Valley lettuce plantings while warm weather ended the Yuma season early, leaving a supply gap at the April 2023 desert-to-Salinas transition.

event_name: Salmonella Thompson outbreak linked to Gills Onions diced onions
description: Gills Onions recalled fresh diced onions on October 23, 2023 and CDC linked them to a Salmonella Thompson outbreak (80 cases in 23 states); declared over December 4, 2023.

event_name: Salmonella outbreak linked to cucumbers
description: FDA and CDC announced a multistate Salmonella Africana outbreak potentially linked to cucumbers on June 12, 2024, later combined with a Salmonella Braenderup outbreak traced to Florida growers (551 cases in 34 states and DC); declared over August 22, 2024.

event_name: USDA pauses avocado inspections in Michoacan
description: Two USDA employees were attacked in Michoacan on June 14, 2024; the US suspended avocado and mango inspections there (announced June 18) and began a gradual resumption around June 21.

event_name: Viral cucumber salad trend
description: TikTok creator Logan Moffitt's cucumber salad videos went viral from July 2024; widely reported cucumber sell-outs (e.g. Iceland) in August 2024.

event_name: McDonald's E. coli outbreak traced to slivered onions
description: CDC announced the McDonald's Quarter Pounder E. coli O157:H7 outbreak on Oct 22, 2024; Taylor Farms recalled yellow onions on Oct 25; outbreak declared over Dec 3, 2024.

event_name: Fall 2024 lettuce shortage at Salinas-desert transition
description: An extended October 2024 heat wave, then strong winds and cold in the Arizona/California desert, cut lettuce weights as Salinas wound down and the Yuma start was delayed; Markon expected elevated markets through early December.

event_name: SunFed cucumber recall (Salmonella Typhimurium)
description: SunFed Produce recalled American/slicer cucumbers grown by Agrotato (Sonora, Mexico) on Nov 27, 2024 after a Salmonella Typhimurium outbreak (68 cases in 19 states by Nov 26); CDC's final update is dated January 8, 2025.

event_name: 25% US tariff on Mexican imports
description: The US imposed a 25% tariff on all imports from Mexico on March 4, 2025; it was lifted for USMCA-qualifying goods from March 7, and Mexican avocado exporters paused much of their harvest while the tariff was in force.

event_name: 25% US tariff on Mexican and Canadian imports
description: The US imposed 25% tariffs on all imports from Mexico and Canada on March 4, 2025, before exempting USMCA-qualifying goods from March 7; Mexican produce growers reported falling orders.

event_name: 25% US tariff on Mexican and Canadian imports
description: The US imposed 25% tariffs on all imports from Mexico and Canada on March 4, 2025, before exempting USMCA-qualifying goods from March 7; Mexican produce growers reported falling orders.

event_name: 25% US tariff on Mexican and Canadian imports
description: The US imposed 25% tariffs on all imports from Mexico and Canada on March 4, 2025, before exempting USMCA-qualifying goods from March 7; Mexican produce growers reported falling orders.

event_name: Salmonella Montevideo outbreak linked to Bedner Growers cucumbers
description: FDA and CDC linked a Salmonella Montevideo outbreak to whole cucumbers grown by Bedner Growers (Florida) and distributed by Fresh Start Produce Sales, which recalled them on May 19, 2025; 69 cases in 21 states, declared over June 30, 2025.

event_name: Fall 2025 Salinas lettuce shortage
description: Heat, rain and humidity, together with bottom rot, mildew, insect and disease pressure, lowered lettuce weights and yields in the Salinas Valley in fall 2025; Markon expected elevated markets until the desert season ramped up in mid-to-late November.

event_name: Florida freeze cucumber shortage
description: Repeated freezes in Florida in January 2026, a warm winter that raised disease pressure in Mexico and freeze-delayed planting in Georgia left a large cucumber production gap; relief was not expected until the late-April Georgia and May California crops.

event_name: Cyclospora outbreak linked to Taylor Farms de Mexico iceberg lettuce
description: CDC and FDA linked a Cyclospora outbreak, first reported through Taco Bell customers, to processed iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico, which recalled all iceberg sourced from central Mexico on July 17, 2026; 12,883 cases in 21 states and 2 deaths, declared over September 11, 2026.

event_name: US suspends avocado inspections in Michoacan
description: The US suspended all government operations in Michoacan, including USDA avocado export inspections, on August 5, 2026 after a security threat; inspections partly resumed at 45 packing houses on August 10 and fully resumed on August 13.
